title: Split GPU coordinator from capacity scheduler and clean up lifecycle reconciliation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
The current GPU fleet controller combines capacity planning, node lifecycle state machine, and lease reconciliation into a single reconciler. This monolith has caused sporadic scale-up spikes, race conditions during node termination, and brittle code paths that make upgrades risky.

Goal:
Refactor to cleanly separate (1) the GPU Coordinator (event-driven node lifecycle and lease handling) from (2) the Capacity Scheduler (placement, bin-packing, and scaling decisions). This should reduce contention in reconciliation loops, make unit testing simpler, and pave the way for the k8s client upgrade.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Extract GPU Coordinator component responsible for node state transitions, graceful drain/termination handshake, and local lease reconciliation.
- Simplify Capacity Scheduler to a deterministic, idempotent decision engine: accepts cluster snapshot + demand signal, emits scaling/move intents.
- Replace the inlined leader-election helper with the new cluster-leader library and bump k8s client libs to v0.26.
- Introduce a thin async queue between scheduler outputs and coordinator actions to provide backpressure and retry semantics.
- Add end-to-end tests that simulate transient cloud API errors, preemption, and workload bursts.
- Instrument key metrics: coordinator_queue_length, scheduler_decision_latency_ms, lease_reconcile_failures.
- Document rollout plan and rollback toggles (feature flag: fleet_refactor_v1).

Non-goals:
- Address caching/batching runtime improvements (separate project).
- Rework the external autoscaler API surface (compatibility must be preserved).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Unit and integration test coverage for coordinator state transitions > 85%.
- No increase in median scale-up latency in canary cluster (target: <= 5% regression).
- All existing production incidents related to double-allocations are reproducible in test harness and fixed.
- k8s client and leader-election dependency upgraded without breaking rolling upgrades.
- Feature flag enables easy rollback to previous reconciler in prod with zero customer impact.
